title: Unveiling and Mitigating Bias in Large Language Model Recommendations: A Path to Fairness

bias_targets.methodology: Generating movie, book, and song recommendations via LLMs for male and female user profiles, classifying the output genres, and analyzing the distribution differences using Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD) and fairness metrics like Statistical Parity Difference (SPD), Disparate Impact (DI), and Equal Opportunity Difference (EOD).

Comparing the distribution of recommended item genres provided to user profiles of different ages (e.g., 20-year-old vs. 60-year-old) using normalized genre fractions, divergence metrics, and fairness indicators.

Evaluating disparities in recommended genres (e.g., fiction vs. biographies) across different user professions by varying occupations in prompts and applying classifier-based fairness metrics to the outputs.

Prompting LLMs with user profiles from different representative global regions (e.g., North America, South Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa) and analyzing the resulting recommendation genre distributions to identify cultural stereotypes and skewed exposure.

Introducing 'affluent' versus 'impoverished' contextual descriptors into user prompts (Context-Based Generation) and measuring the resulting shifts and disparities in the recommended genres using fairness metrics.
Adding 'introvert' versus 'extrovert' behavioral traits to user profiles in prompts to measure the disparities and biases in the generated recommendation genres.
Including 'rural' versus 'metropolitan' living area contexts in user prompts and quantifying the differences in the recommended item genres using statistical parity and divergence metrics.
